title: Referral pathway from oncologists to physiotherapists
problem: Many patients who could benefit from exercise are never referred. Oncologists do not always know who to refer to, and the referral takes time during a short visit.
hypothesis: If the referral is one click in the patient record and has a named receiver, more eligible patients will be referred within two weeks of starting treatment.
nextStep: Count referrals for four more weeks and compare with the same period last year.

title: Time allocation for digital consultations
problem: Digital consultations are booked in the gaps between physical visits. Staff feel they do them in addition to their normal work.
hypothesis: If each physiotherapist has two fixed 45-minute blocks per week for digital consultations, fewer sessions are cancelled and staff report less stress.
nextStep: Agree with the unit manager on which weeks to test fixed blocks.

title: Equipment for physiotherapists in rural areas
problem: Physiotherapists in small clinics do not have a tablet, a camera stand or a quiet room for video sessions.
nextStep: Ask three rural clinics what equipment they have today.

title: Patient information in local languages
problem: The exercise app and the information leaflets are in English or in one national language only. Some patients do not understand the instructions.
hypothesis: If patients receive a one-page instruction in their own language, more of them complete the first digital session without help.
nextStep: Ask the patient group to review the Lithuanian and Polish drafts.

title: Shared start-up checklist for new exercise oncology sites
problem: Each new site starts from zero and repeats the same mistakes, for example forgetting to involve the IT department early.
hypothesis: If new sites follow a shared checklist, they can offer the first digital session sooner.
nextStep: Share the checklist with associated partners.
learned: The checklist worked best when one named person at the new site owned it. Sites wanted fewer items, so we reduced the list from 31 to 18. Involving the IT department in the first week saved the most time.

title: A named person who finds eligible patients
problem: Nobody has the task of finding patients who could join the exercise programme, so inclusion depends on chance.
hypothesis: If one staff member checks the clinic list every week, the number of patients who are offered the programme will double.
nextStep: Describe the role in half a page so that other sites can copy it.

title: Short video that introduces the exercise app to patients
problem: Staff spend 15 to 20 minutes explaining the app to each new patient.
hypothesis: If patients watch a three-minute video before the first visit, staff need less than five minutes for the introduction.
nextStep: Record a first version with a phone and show it to five patients.

title: Digital readiness self-check for clinics
problem: Clinics do not know if they are ready to offer digital rehabilitation, and the existing questionnaires are long and technical.
hypothesis: If a clinic can answer 12 simple questions in 15 minutes, it can see its three most important gaps.
nextStep: Choose the 12 questions together with two clinics.

title: Practice Lab: joint online case discussions for physiotherapists
problem: Physiotherapists who work with cancer patients are often alone in their clinic and have nobody to discuss difficult cases with.
hypothesis: If physiotherapists from different countries meet online for 45 minutes every month, they feel more confident in adapting exercise to treatment side effects.
nextStep: Hold the third session and ask participants what they changed in practice.

title: Involving patient advocacy groups in service design
problem: Patient groups are informed about new services when they are finished, not asked while they are being designed.
nextStep: Wait for the stakeholder map before choosing which groups to invite.

title: Back-up plan when a key staff member is away
problem: At several sites the digital service stops when one person is ill or on leave.
hypothesis: If two staff members are trained for each task and a one-page routine exists, no patient session is cancelled because of staff absence.
nextStep: List the tasks that only one person can do today.

title: Follow-up call after the first digital session
problem: Some patients stop after the first digital session and we do not know why.
nextStep: Call five patients who stopped and ask what happened.
